summary: Recorded the blueprint-only Git baseline, local toolchain, integrity/security inspection, compatibility risks, and a preservation-first Rails initialization path; ignored the tracker runtime lock.

Initialized the Rails 8.1.3.1 PostgreSQL application with Ruby 3.4.10/Bundler 4.0.14 runtime pins, Hotwire/Tailwind, Solid Cache/Queue/Cable, reproducible setup documentation, environment-name template, and baseline contract tests.
Documented and enforced modular-monolith ownership, explicit public APIs, dependency allowlists, shared primitive locations, naming rules, and reviewed exception handling.

Added typed fail-fast configuration for development, test, staging and production; separated runtime/credential secrets from public YAML settings; integrated parameter/header/URL/event redaction; documented configuration inventory and rotation.

Hardened tracker catalog/state/result validation, aligned the result JSON schema, expanded isolated mutation/concurrency/corruption tests, documented honest recovery, and added a read-only CI tracker job.

Created governed ADR lifecycle/index/template and PR risk checklist, added an automated ADR link/metadata guardrail, reviewed all ten decisions against the repository, and reconciled the complete module catalog.

Configured PostgreSQL-only primary, queue, cache and cable databases with local colocation and independent protected-environment URLs; added bounded pools and capacity validation, timeouts, application names, advisory-lock configuration, reversible pgcrypto enablement, UUID/bigint policy, strict SELECT 1 health checks, clean setup documentation, CI wiring and negative/real-connection tests.

Activated Solid Queue and Solid Cache across Rails runtimes and Solid Cable in development/staging/production; added a single-source queue/priority registry, exact isolated worker role allowlists, scheduler ownership enforcement, bounded retry/discard behavior, safe recurring cleanup, disposable cache/cable limits, a real PostgreSQL smoke job and operational runbook.

Built accessible public and authenticated Rails shells with responsive native navigation, reusable explicit-local partials, Tailwind component tokens, an honest home/sign-in/dashboard scaffold, server-rendered validation, Turbo frame enhancement, focused error handling, reduced motion and frontend guidance.

Established a reproducible quality pipeline covering Rails Omakase Ruby style, ERB safety and embedded Ruby linting, JavaScript module syntax, strict YAML/JSON and duplicate-key validation, blueprint and architecture contracts, Tailwind compilation, Brakeman, importmap and locked-gem advisory audits; documented time-bounded waiver governance and fixed existing template findings.

Created reusable deterministic Minitest support for clocks, UUIDs, encrypted-value checks, exact-body signatures, scoped Current tenancy, tenant isolation, jobs, idempotency, permission/audit/usage decisions and strict provider fakes; added a loopback-only malicious HTTP fixture, organized test layers, hardened headless Chrome failure artifacts and documented suite tiers and seed reproduction.

Added a least-privilege split GitHub Actions pipeline with immutable action and service pins lockfile caching tracker quality Rails security browser and production image gates bounded failure artifacts branch-aware concurrency an aggregate merge check automated policy validation and local reproduction documentation

Implemented a stable domain error taxonomy safe JSON and HTML error mapping structured allowlisted events keyed tenant identifiers request and ActiveJob trace correlation fail-safe context clearing expanded nested payload header query and URL redaction operator cause reporting and observability governance documentation

Implemented dependency-free JSON liveness role-aware timeout-bounded PostgreSQL readiness sanitized no-store release provenance a private aggregate Solid Queue heartbeat snapshot production probes for all three endpoints and Kamal/load-balancer operating documentation

Implemented the application-owned Identity boundary with PostgreSQL-backed opaque sessions, keyed token and metadata digests, absolute and idle expiry, request-scoped Current identity, guarded controllers, safe local returns, rotation, logout revocation, secure environment-aware cookies, and redacted security events.

Completed the durable Identity model with citext-normalized users, stable provider-subject identities, bounded allowlisted provider profiles, strengthened session constraints, and 15-minute one-time OAuth transactions using keyed state/nonce/PKCE digests, authenticated PKCE encryption, attempt metadata, and PostgreSQL row-lock consumption.

Defined a provider-neutral Identity adapter contract with immutable redacted values, protocol-specific Google OIDC and GitHub OAuth semantics, exact endpoint/redirect allowlists, bounded TLS HTTP behavior, deterministic failure fakes, side-effect-free stable-subject account resolution, and a provider addition runbook.

Implemented hardened Google OIDC authorization start with high-entropy state/nonce/PKCE, encrypted one-time transaction storage, safe return paths, explicitly recent-session-bound link intents, PostgreSQL-serialized rate/outstanding limits, secure response headers, correlation-only observability, configuration, UI, documentation, and migration constraints.

Completed Google OIDC callback handling with one-time PostgreSQL state consumption, exact non-retried PKCE code exchange, strict RS256/JWKS and issuer/audience/azp/time/nonce validation, bounded key caching and rotation, stable-subject account creation or explicit recent-session linking, verified-email collision policy, session issuance/rotation, safe redirects, redacted categorized audit failures, configuration and synchronized documentation.

Implemented the GitHub OAuth sign-in adapter with exact PKCE authorization and callback contracts, bounded GitHub API access, stable numeric subject identity, verified-primary-email policy, shared provider-neutral account transition, collision-safe explicit linking, UI/fakes, audit-safe errors, and documentation.

Implemented explicit provider linking confirmation and account-security management with provider/session-bound signed confirmations, one-time recent-session OAuth linking, privacy-safe collision handling, PostgreSQL-locked unlinking, atomic session rotation, last-identity protection, safe metadata UI, request-ID diagnostics, audit events, concurrency defenses, and synchronized operations/security documentation.

Implemented privacy-minimal session inventory and management with broad client/device observations, current-session marking, recent-authenticated single/all-other revocation, anti-enumeration and CSRF controls, reusable identity/ownership/role/compromise risk hooks, bounded maintenance cleanup, structured events, real PostgreSQL concurrency coverage, and synchronized operations documentation.

Implemented accessible authentication and first-run onboarding UI with configured-provider availability, privacy-preserving actionable OAuth errors, local account profile editing, explicit no-organization/invited/returning state handling, authenticated navigation, and system coverage for the four required user journeys.

Added PostgreSQL-backed fixed-window authentication rate limits for OAuth initiation, callback failures, session management and account-security actions using HMAC-protected IP/session keys; generic Retry-After responses; bounded auth metrics; hourly cleanup; a dedicated CI security command; and consolidated protocol, redaction, collision, fixation and concurrency regressions.

Added constrained organization, durable ownership and membership aggregates; atomic owner creation; verified request/job tenant context; safe active-membership switcher; lifecycle/rename audit; tenant isolation helpers and documentation.
Added accessible organization creation and owner-only settings; safe active-membership switching; suspended-state presentation; controlled historical slug redirects and reserved-slug enforcement.

Added durable invited active suspended and removed membership states; locked lifecycle operations; last-owner protection; immediate session revocation; hashed actor/subject audit; paginated member UI and retained attribution.

Added organization-scoped teams with composite tenant FKs; locked create rename archive and idempotent membership operations; bounded paginated UI/search; archive semantics and an immutable authorization-principals boundary.

Implemented owner-managed, one-time organization invitations with HMAC-only token storage, encrypted browser handoff, exact verified-provider-email acceptance, atomic membership activation, revoke/resend/expiry lifecycle, HMAC-keyed rate limits, audit events, multi-invite onboarding, accessible screens and synchronous mail previews/fakes.

Implemented the governed 57-permission catalog and eight immutable system-role templates with explicit risk/scope metadata, strict YAML semantics, PostgreSQL ownership constraints, idempotent advisory-locked synchronization, rename/removal protection, immutable checksum revisions, db:seed integration and a development matrix report that is tested against the blueprint documentation.

Implemented tenant-safe membership/team role assignments at organization, project and property scopes; allow-only union/inheritance semantics; grant-subset and self-escalation checks; deterministic lifecycle filtering; atomic invitation role application; hashed audit context; indexed effective-permission resolution; and concurrent idempotent assign/revoke operations.

Implemented an immutable authorization request/resource contract, explainable fail-closed decision engine with scoped direct/team provenance, owner-only protections, immediate privilege-change visibility, bounded high-risk denial audit events, and reusable controller/view/job/domain policy adapters while keeping RBAC independent from plans, entitlements, quotas and billing.

Applied explicit permission declarations to every tenant controller action, actor-bound domain authorization proofs, fail-closed UI hints, bounded JSON denial contracts, execution-time job reauthorization policies, a governed route/domain/job inventory and automated coverage checks.
